title: Articles of Association — contract, alteration and indoor management

content.overview: Articles regulate internal management and bind the company and members under s. 10 as if signed by them, subject to the Act.
content.glance: Articles regulate internal management and bind the company and members under s. 10 as if signed by them, subject to the Act.
content.study: Section 5 allows articles, and entrenchment provisions alterable only by a stricter procedure. Table F applies so far as not excluded. Alteration is by special resolution under s. 14. Articles cannot override the Act (s. 6). As between members they are a statutory contract on membership rights, not a source of outsider rights merely because a non-member is named. Indoor management, from Royal British Bank v. Turquand, protects outsiders dealing in good faith as to internal compliance, but not where the transaction is ultra vires or the outsider had notice.
